title: Build Your First Azure Landing Zone
description: Prepare a small Azure practice foundation, upload pretend inventory data, test recovery and clean up.
baseline: lab.example.test · Azure portal · small learning foundation, not a production Azure Landing Zones deployment · metered storage · $25 monthly training goal, not a cap
prerequisite: Before you start, you will need an active Azure training subscription and permission to create resources there. We will build this in the Azure portal, one piece at a time. Nothing is created or charged by opening this class.
supplies: An active Azure training subscription and permission to create the dedicated lab resources.
Permission to assign Storage Blob Data Contributor at the lab storage account, or a lab administrator who can do it.
A Windows 10 PC, a modern browser, Windows PowerShell and a few private lab notes.
Your monthly training cost worksheet and a planned cleanup date. This is a pay-as-you-go lab, not a guaranteed free offer.

lessons.title: Understand Your Landing Zone
lessons.description: Choose a small Azure practice space and check permissions and costs before building it.
lessons.what: Think of a landing zone as a prepared place for your application to move into. We will build a small practice foundation, then give it a tiny pretend business file.
lessons.why: A company needs agreed rules for identity, cost, networks and data before its applications arrive. Our small lab teaches those decisions without deploying a full company platform.
needs: An active Azure training subscription you are allowed to use.
Your browser, Windows 10 PC and a place to save short lab notes.
Permission to create the lab resources and assign the required data role; ask your tenant administrator if you do not have it.
bestPractices: Keep your lab notes beside the portal and use only the dedicated practice resources.
Before selecting Create, read the subscription, resource name and paid options one more time.
commonMistakes: Using the picture’s example names instead of your own CloudSeam values.
Moving on before the expected check passes.

troubleshooting.problem: I cannot create a budget or assign a role.
troubleshooting.fix: Your account may have resource access without billing or role-assignment access. Ask the training subscription owner for the narrow permission needed; do not use a production subscription instead.

lessons.pass: Explain the four boxes, show your training subscription name privately, and record your spending review point.
lessons.exercise: Explain the four boxes, show your training subscription name privately, and record your spending review point.

quiz.question: Does the budget stop Azure at $25?
options: No. It warns you; you still need to monitor and clean up.
quiz.explanation: Budgets notify you. Resources and subscription-level plans can keep charging until you remove or disable them.

steps.title: Draw the small version first
actions: Write: “I am preparing a place for CloudSeam’s pretend inventory file.”
Use the diagram to name the subscription, resource group, network and storage account.
Write “learning foundation” at the top. A resource group alone is not a production Azure landing zone. Companies also design management groups, policy, monitoring and shared services.
steps.expected: You can explain what each box does. Microsoft calls the application environment a workload landing zone; this lab is a reduced practice example.

screenshot.title: What we are building
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Check where you are signed in
actions: Open portal.azure.com and search for Subscriptions.
Select only your training subscription. Copy its name and subscription ID to your private notes.
Open Access control (IAM) → View my access. Check your resource-creation permissions and whether you can assign roles at the planned storage account scope.
Keep lab.example.test as the Windows lab domain. Do not rename your Entra tenant or add public DNS records for this exercise.
steps.expected: Your notes identify the exact training subscription and the person who can grant the storage data role.

screenshot.title: Check your account before you start
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Set a review point for spending
steps.where: Azure portal → Cost Management + Billing → Cost Management
actions: Choose the training subscription scope and open Budgets → Add.
Create a monthly cost budget named cloudseam-training with amount 25 in your billing currency; use USD only if your account is billed in USD.
Add an actual-cost alert at 40% and an email you read. For a USD25 budget, that is an early review at USD10.
Check current Blob Storage pricing and your existing subscription costs. Leave paid security add-ons off for this lab; existing subscription-level plans may still charge.
steps.expected: You have a saved budget and an alert recipient. An alert is a reminder, not a hard cap; delayed usage can appear after cleanup.

screenshot.title: Set the cost boundary before building
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

lessons.title: Create Your Practice Resource Group
lessons.description: Create a clearly named home for the lab and label it so you can find and remove it later.
lessons.what: Let’s give all the practice pieces one easy-to-find home. A resource group is a management folder for related Azure resources.
lessons.why: Keeping this exercise together makes cleanup much easier. It also helps you avoid deleting resources from another class.
needs: Keep your selected subscription and cleanup date in your notes.
bestPractices: Keep your lab notes beside the portal and use only the dedicated practice resources.
Before selecting Create, read the subscription, resource name and paid options one more time.
commonMistakes: Using the picture’s example names instead of your own CloudSeam values.
Moving on before the expected check passes.

troubleshooting.fix: Open it and confirm it belongs only to this exercise. If it contains other work, choose a new unique lab group name and use that name throughout.

lessons.pass: Reopen the group and show its subscription, region and four tags. Explain why ExpiresOn will not delete it automatically.
lessons.exercise: Reopen the group and show its subscription, region and four tags. Explain why ExpiresOn will not delete it automatically.

quiz.question: What makes an ExpiresOn tag reduce cost?
options: Azure always deletes the resource on that date
You use it to find expired resources and actually clean them up
quiz.explanation: The tag is a label. A person or separately configured automation must act on it.

steps.title: Create the group
actions: Search for Resource groups, then select Create.
Select the training subscription you recorded. Name the group rg-cloudseam-lz-lab.
Choose a region available to you, such as East US, and record it. Use that same region for the network and storage account.
Select Review + create, then Create. Open Go to resource group.
steps.expected: The group overview shows rg-cloudseam-lz-lab in the intended subscription.

screenshot.title: Create a resource group
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Add the lab labels
actions: Open Tags in the group menu.
Add Environment=Lab, Project=SONIC-Academy and Owner=your approved non-secret learner ID.
Add ExpiresOn with the day you plan to remove the lab, using YYYY-MM-DD. Select Apply.
Do not put passwords, tokens, email addresses or private customer information in tags.
steps.expected: The saved tags identify this lab and its cleanup date.

screenshot.title: Label the practice resources
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Know what the labels do
actions: Write one sentence: “Tags help me find resources; cleanup is what stops their charges.”
Remember that group tags do not automatically appear on the resources inside it. We will add the same tags when creating the network and storage account.
Check the empty resource list. There should be no VM, gateway or other paid surprise in this new group.
steps.expected: You can find the group by name and tags, and its Resources list is empty.

screenshot.title: Why tags can help reduce costs
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

lessons.title: Prepare the Network
lessons.description: Create an empty virtual network and understand how this lab will reach storage.
lessons.what: A virtual network is a private address space for future Azure machines. We will prepare one, but we will not pay to run servers in it.
lessons.why: Separating the network plan from the machines helps you see what each piece does. Blob Storage is its own service; it does not automatically join this network.
needs: Finish Create Your Practice Resource Group.
Check that 10.60.0.0/16 does not overlap any network you plan to connect later. If it does, ask for an unused range and record it.
bestPractices: Keep your lab notes beside the portal and use only the dedicated practice resources.
Before selecting Create, read the subscription, resource name and paid options one more time.
commonMistakes: Using the picture’s example names instead of your own CloudSeam values.
Moving on before the expected check passes.

troubleshooting.problem: Azure says the address range overlaps.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the subnet is inside your VNet range and does not overlap another subnet in this VNet. For future connected networks, choose an approved unused address plan before deployment.

lessons.pass: Record the VNet and subnet names and ranges, and explain why no VM is running in them.
lessons.exercise: Record the VNet and subnet names and ranges, and explain why no VM is running in them.

quiz.question: Did creating the VNet automatically make Blob Storage private to it?
options: No. Storage network access must be configured separately.
Only if both resources use the same tag
quiz.explanation: A storage account is a separate service. A matching resource group or region does not attach it to a VNet.

steps.title: Open the network wizard
actions: Search for Virtual networks and select Create.
Choose your training subscription and rg-cloudseam-lz-lab.
Set the name to vnet-cloudseam-lab and use the region from your notes.
On Security, leave paid Azure Bastion, Azure Firewall and DDoS Network Protection off. Do not add a gateway or a VM.
steps.expected: The wizard names only the empty lab network, with no paid optional appliances selected.

screenshot.title: Reserve a network for future servers
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Set the address space
actions: Set the IPv4 address space to 10.60.0.0/16.
Edit the default subnet or add the single subnet snet-workload with 10.60.1.0/24. Save the subnet.
Add the same four lab tags on Tags.
Open Review + create. Check the subscription, group, region and ranges, then select Create.
steps.expected: Deployment completes. Subnets lists snet-workload at 10.60.1.0/24.

screenshot.title: Check the network before you select Create
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Explain what is connected
actions: Open Connected devices. This new network should have no VM network interfaces.
Open Subnets and check the saved range.
Write: “The network is ready for future servers. Today I upload from my Windows browser to a storage endpoint, not through this empty VNet.”
steps.expected: You can distinguish the empty private network from the authenticated storage upload path.

screenshot.title: Reserve a network for future servers
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

lessons.title: Create Protected Storage
lessons.description: Create a small storage account, limit its network access and give yourself file permissions.
lessons.what: Now we need a place for the pretend inventory file. A storage account holds files as objects called blobs. A container groups those blobs.
lessons.why: We want the file to be reachable by you, while anonymous visitors and unrelated networks are turned away.
needs: Be on a connection with a public IPv4 address the storage firewall can allow. A VPN or changing home address can require an updated rule.
bestPractices: Keep your lab notes beside the portal and use only the dedicated practice resources.
Before selecting Create, read the subscription, resource name and paid options one more time.
commonMistakes: Using the picture’s example names instead of your own CloudSeam values.
Moving on before the expected check passes.

troubleshooting.fix: Check the tenant and storage account first. Check the client public IPv4 rule, then Storage Blob Data Contributor and its scope. Wait for role propagation and refresh. A management Contributor role alone does not grant Entra blob-data access.

lessons.pass: Show the private container, Microsoft Entra authentication method, client IP rule and storage-scoped data role.
lessons.exercise: Show the private container, Microsoft Entra authentication method, client IP rule and storage-scoped data role.

quiz.question: What is required to upload a file here?
options: Both an allowed network source and an authorized identity
quiz.explanation: The firewall checks the source network. Microsoft Entra and the data role check who you are and what you may do.

steps.title: Choose the storage settings
actions: Select your training subscription, rg-cloudseam-lz-lab and the same region.
Use a globally unique name such as stcloudseamlab followed by your own lowercase letters and numbers. Storage names use 3–24 lowercase letters and digits; no dots or hyphens.
Choose Standard performance, general-purpose v2 where offered, and Locally-redundant storage (LRS). Use Hot for this tiny active lab.
On Advanced, require secure transfer, set minimum TLS to 1.2, disable anonymous blob access and choose Microsoft Entra authorization as the portal default. Leave hierarchical set of names off.
Disable shared-key authorization using Allow storage account key access where the wizard offers that setting. Do not enable paid Defender for Storage. Add the lab tags.
steps.expected: The planned account has the correct name, Standard LRS storage and no paid optional protection selected.

screenshot.title: Storage account setup tabs
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Restrict the upload route
actions: Use public network access with access limited to selected networks / IP addresses.

Add your current public client IPv4 address using the portal’s Add your client IP option. Do not choose all networks. In the saved Networking settings, remove any extra IP/network rules and leave trusted-service/resource-instance exceptions off for this standalone lab.
Do not add a private endpoint or paid gateway. This exercise uses authenticated HTTPS over the restricted public endpoint.
If this wizard cannot add the client rule, create with public network access Disabled, then open Networking and enable Selected networks with your client IP before trying to upload.
Review the chosen settings and select Create. When deployment completes, confirm the saved Networking rules.
steps.expected: The account allows your current client IP only. Its endpoint is public, but its data is not anonymously accessible.

screenshot.title: Allow only your current home connection
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Grant your account file access
actions: Select Add → Add role assignment. Search for Storage Blob Data Contributor and select it.
On Members, choose User, group, or service principal → Select members. Select your own training sign-in.
Review + assign at this storage account scope. Do not grant the role across your whole subscription.

You also need at least Reader management access to browse the account in the portal; the resource creator’s Contributor access normally already provides that. If role assignment is unavailable, ask the lab administrator.
Allow up to 30 minutes for the data role to take effect, then refresh the portal. Do not fall back to a shared key to hide a permissions problem.
steps.expected: Role assignments lists Storage Blob Data Contributor for your account at the storage account scope.

screenshot.title: Add a role assignment
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Create the private container
steps.where: Your storage account → Data storage → Containers
actions: Select + Container and name it sample-data.
Keep anonymous access level Private (no anonymous access), then create the container.
Open sample-data. Check that the authentication method says Microsoft Entra user account; switch to that method if necessary.
If the data screen is denied, check the current client IP rule and the data role separately. Keep anonymous access disabled.
steps.expected: The empty sample-data container opens using Microsoft Entra authentication. Private here means no anonymous data access; it does not mean a private network endpoint.

screenshot.title: Create a private blob container
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

lessons.title: Upload Your Dummy Data
lessons.description: Create three fake inventory records, upload them and check the downloaded copy.
lessons.what: Let’s give the landing-zone practice space a tiny workload: a file listing three made-up training machines. Nothing here comes from a real company.
lessons.why: Uploading is only half the job. Downloading and checking the contents proves that you put the right file in the right place.
needs: Finish Create Protected Storage and open sample-data.
Your Windows 10 computer and Windows PowerShell; the command below only writes a small local CSV.
bestPractices: Keep your lab notes beside the portal and use only the dedicated practice resources.
Before selecting Create, read the subscription, resource name and paid options one more time.
commonMistakes: Using the picture’s example names instead of your own CloudSeam values.
Moving on before the expected check passes.

troubleshooting.problem: The downloaded file opens as a spreadsheet.
troubleshooting.fix: That is fine, but Notepad shows the exact plain text. Right-click the local file, choose Open with → Notepad, and compare the four lines.

lessons.pass: Show the three fake records in the downloaded copy and explain why a plain URL does not give an anonymous visitor permission.
lessons.exercise: Show the three fake records in the downloaded copy and explain why a plain URL does not give an anonymous visitor permission.

quiz.question: What does dummy data mean here?
options: A safe copy of a customer export
Invented records with no real people or secrets
An account password stored as a CSV
quiz.explanation: Dummy data is invented for practice. It lets you test a process without exposing real information.

steps.title: Create the fake inventory file
actions: Open Windows PowerShell on your Windows 10 host; administrator access is not needed.
If Downloads already has a file named cloudseam-inventory.csv that you want to keep, rename that older file first. This command replaces a same-named file.
Copy and run the command below. It creates cloudseam-inventory.csv in your Downloads folder.
Open the file in Notepad and check for the header plus three made-up device rows. Do not replace them with real employee or customer details.
steps.expected: Downloads contains a CSV with four lines: one header and three fake devices.

breakdown.meaning: A plain-text table. Commas separate the columns and each line is one row.
Writes this small pretend table to a file on your Windows computer. It does not upload anything to Azure.

screenshot.title: Make a pretend inventory file
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.command:
@'
asset_id,device_name,os,owner_group
LAB-001,APP01,Windows Server 2019,Training
LAB-002,ALMA01,AlmaLinux 9,Training
LAB-003,DC01,Windows Server 2019,Training
'@ | Set-Content -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\cloudseam-inventory.csv" -Encoding UTF8

steps.title: Upload into the container
steps.where: Azure portal → Your storage account → Containers → sample-data
actions: Check Microsoft Entra user account is the data authentication method.
Select Upload → Browse for files. Choose Downloads → cloudseam-inventory.csv.
Keep the blob type as Block blob and do not enable overwrite if an unrelated file already uses this name.
Select Upload and wait for completion. Refresh the list if needed.
steps.expected: The container lists cloudseam-inventory.csv with a nonzero size and a recent modified time.

screenshot.title: Upload a local file to Blob Storage
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Download and compare
actions: Select the blob, then Download. Save it to a new folder so it does not replace your original.
Open the downloaded file in Notepad. Compare its column names and all three rows with the original.
For an extra check, run Get-FileHash on each actual file path in PowerShell. Their SHA256 values should match.
Write down the container name, blob name and the result of your comparison.
steps.expected: Both copies contain the same header and three fake records. Matching SHA256 values, if checked, show the downloaded bytes match the original.

screenshot.title: Download a blob
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Test the anonymous boundary
actions: From the blob properties, copy only its normal URL. Do not create a shared access signature (SAS) or copy an access token.
Open a new private browser window where you are not signed in. Paste the plain URL.
The file should not download anonymously. Azure may show an authorization error or an unhelpful not-found response.
Close the private window. Return to your signed-in portal and confirm you can still download through your authorized session.
steps.expected: The plain URL does not allow an anonymous download, while your authorized portal access still works.

screenshot.title: Microsoft Entra data authorization
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

lessons.title: Recover the File and Clean Up
lessons.description: Practise recovering a deleted blob, then remove the lab and check remaining costs.
lessons.what: Before we finish, let’s prove you can recover from a small mistake. We will delete only the pretend file, bring it back and then remove the practice resources.
lessons.why: A recovery plan is useful only when you test it. Cleanup matters too: stopping a computer would not stop storage charges, and this lab does not even have a VM.
needs: Keep a local copy of the CSV. You will delete only this exercise’s fake file and dedicated resource group.
bestPractices: Keep your lab notes beside the portal and use only the dedicated practice resources.
Before selecting Create, read the subscription, resource name and paid options one more time.
commonMistakes: Using the picture’s example names instead of your own CloudSeam values.
Moving on before the expected check passes.

troubleshooting.problem: I cannot restore the blob or delete the group.
troubleshooting.fix: For the blob, confirm soft delete was enabled before deletion, retention has not expired and versioning is off. For group deletion, check for a lock or a policy denial and ask the lab administrator; do not bypass organizational controls.

lessons.pass: Recover the fake file successfully, then show that the lab group is deleted and record a follow-up subscription cost check.
lessons.exercise: Recover the fake file successfully, then show that the lab group is deleted and record a follow-up subscription cost check.

quiz.question: What does deleting the lab resource group remove?
options: Only resources in that group; other resources and subscription plans need their own review
quiz.explanation: Resource-group deletion has a specific scope. Subscription plans, licenses and resources elsewhere are separate.

steps.title: Turn on the short recovery window
steps.where: Your storage account → Data management → Data protection
actions: Enable soft delete for blobs and set retention to 7 days. Save the setting before deleting anything.
Keep blob versioning and point-in-time restore off for this small exercise; the restore steps below use soft delete without versioning.
Wait for the saved configuration to show 7 days. Soft-deleted data still uses storage during retention.
steps.expected: Blob soft delete is enabled for seven days. You have not yet deleted the test file.

screenshot.title: Configure blob soft delete
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Delete only the pretend file
actions: Select only cloudseam-inventory.csv. Check the name before choosing Delete.
Confirm the single-file deletion, then refresh the container.
Turn on Show deleted blobs, or Show active and deleted blobs if that is the label you see.
Select the deleted CSV. Its status should say Deleted.
steps.expected: The fake CSV is marked Deleted and remains visible with the deleted-items view enabled.

screenshot.title: Show deleted blobs
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Bring it back and prove it opens
actions: Select Undelete. Refresh the container and turn off the deleted-items filter if needed.
Open the active CSV and download it into another new local folder.
Check the three fake device rows again. If you never enabled soft delete before deletion, stop: this recovery path will not work; re-upload the safe local CSV and repeat in order.
Write: “Soft delete protects this blob for seven days; it is not a separate backup of my whole Azure environment.”
steps.expected: The CSV is active again and its three rows are readable in the downloaded copy.

screenshot.title: Restore a deleted blob
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.

steps.title: Remove this lab and review the bill
actions: Save your private notes and local CSV first. Open the group and read every resource name.
Delete the group only if it contains just this lab’s network and storage account. Enter the group name when asked and confirm deletion.
Wait for deletion to finish, then check that those two resources no longer appear in All resources. Do not delete resources from other classes.
Open Cost Management → Cost analysis at your training subscription scope. Filter by the lab group or tags and review charges after billing data updates.
Check separately for any paid subscription-level Defender plans, licenses or resources outside this group. A deleted group does not disable them.
steps.expected: The lab resources are gone. You have a follow-up cost check scheduled; a delayed charge can still arrive for usage that occurred before deletion.

screenshot.title: Delete only the practice resource group
screenshot.instructions: Compare this guide with the written settings and check the result in your own subscription.
